reason: E3 directly links VEC to phase stability prediction, supporting the VEC premise. E1 supports that single-phase solid solutions can be stable at high temperatures. However, no cited evidence supports the central premise that configurational entropy maximization governs stability, nor that element interactions influence configurational entropy in the claimed way; E2 discusses chemical clustering, which contradicts the idea of a stable single-phase driven by entropy maximization.
premises: Configurational entropy maximization governs structural and chemical stability in high-entropy nanoalloys.
Valence electron concentration (VEC) influences configurational entropy and phase stability.
Interaction between constituent elements influences configurational entropy.
Single solid solution phases are stable at high temperatures in these alloys.
